title: Onset of Northern Hemisphere glaciation
summary: Around 2.7 million years ago, large ice sheets began to build across the Northern Hemisphere. One study of a western subarctic Pacific sediment core links the start to warmer late summers and cooler winters that supplied snow to northern North America. Another places the intensification across the Pliocene-Pleistocene transition, 2.58 million years ago.

uncertainty.note: Sources give both about 2.7 Ma and 2.58 Ma for the intensification; the range spans both.

as_recorded.value: the timing of the onset of significant Northern Hemisphere glaciation 2.7 million years ago
